text:
Pius Suter has four goals in 17 games for St. Louis, including a late one that spoiled a shutout bid against the Rangers, and he's become a useful penalty-killing depth forward in his second season with the Blues.

The goals are slightly ahead of the chances (four on 2.5 expected, the quality of his chances), and the recent stretch has been thin: two points in his last ten games and ice time down a minute. St. Louis has 46% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, a little worse than without him.

Last season was better than the box score said. Evolving-Hockey had his team creating noticeably more with him on the ice (87th percentile among forwards), with most of his value coming on the penalty kill, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting 2.1 shots per 60 off passes across the slot or from behind the net. He's undrafted, out of Zurich's ZSC Lions. Our projection sees about 15 goals.
